platform.name: android
platform.units: dp for layout, sp for type
platform.tokenSource: app/src/main/java/app/tutti/ui/Theme.kt (TuttiColors, Type, Motion); dish inks in app/src/main/java/app/tutti/model/Recipes.kt

numeral.purpose: The Conduct countdown only, in its own slot beside the instruction.

display.purpose: One screen statement under the disc.

headline-stage.purpose: The current instruction on Conduct, up to two lines, announced as a live region.

time.purpose: Cue times, Finale readings, the tempo marking, and numerals printed on disc labels.

title.purpose: Row titles and the Programme summary.

body.purpose: Instructions and explanations, capped at 360dp wide.

button.purpose: Pill text, Conduct instrument names, switch label.

wordmark.purpose: "Tutti" at the top left of Programme and Finale.

label.purpose: Uppercase tags, track badges, status, and disc-label sub-lettering.

shadows.name: disc-falloff
shadows.value: radial-gradient(circle, rgba(0,0,0,0.22) 0%, rgba(0,0,0,0.22) 80%, transparent 100%); radius 1.12 of disc radius, offset y 0.04 of radius

shadows.name: pivot-falloff
shadows.value: radial-gradient(circle, rgba(0,0,0,0.16) 0%, rgba(0,0,0,0.16) 80%, transparent 100%); radius 26dp, offset 2dp 4dp

shadows.name: sleeve-lift
shadows.value: Compose shadow elevation 1dp at rest, 6dp chosen, 4dp corners (approx. 0 1px 2px rgba(0,0,0,0.2) / 0 4px 10px rgba(0,0,0,0.22))
shadows.purpose: The chosen sleeve rises as its record slides out; the only Material elevation.

shadows.name: vinyl-sheen
shadows.value: sweep-gradient: transparent 0, white 9% at 0.07, transparent 0.16, transparent 0.55, white 6% at 0.61, transparent 0.70
shadows.purpose: Fixed light on the vinyl that stays put while the disc turns.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: Motion.out. Anything responding to the cook: presses, screen entry, label ink swap, flashes, spin-down.

motion.name: ease-in-out
motion.purpose: Motion.inOut. Things already on screen changing place: needle drop and lift.

motion.name: press
motion.purpose: Every pill and tappable row sinks when pressed.

motion.name: screen-enter
motion.value: fade 240ms + scale from 0.97 over 280ms, 80ms delay, ease-out; exit fade 90ms
motion.purpose: Screen changes; instant when Remove animations is on.

motion.name: ui-state
motion.purpose: Unchosen sleeve fade (to 58%), Conduct label paper swap, panel content fade-in.

motion.name: sleeve-spring
motion.purpose: Record sliding half out of its sleeve, turning 70 degrees.

motion.name: arm-follow
motion.purpose: Tonearm tracking the session in real time.

motion.name: needle-drop
motion.purpose: Tonearm lowering at the start and lifting after the final chord.

motion.name: beat-rotation
motion.value: linear, 45 degrees per beat from the beat clock
motion.purpose: Disc spin and strobe pulse; disabled when Remove animations is on.

motion.name: cue-flash
motion.value: white 30% on the slice, decays over 1400ms ease-out
motion.purpose: A cue firing on its dish's slice.

motion.name: spin-down
motion.value: 70 degrees over 2600ms ease-out; Finale settle 150 degrees over 2200ms
motion.purpose: The record slowing to a stop at the finale.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: animationsEnabled(): no spin, instant needle, instant screen swaps, settled Finale.

narrative.overview:
Dinner is a record you play. Every surface of Tutti is part of one modern deck: a flat aluminum-grey plinth (smoked graphite in the dark theme), a matte black disc pressed with one groove band per dish, a graphite tonearm that tracks inward through the cues, and a single amber cue light that means your hands, now. Time runs inward from the rim to the label, so the needle reaching the label means serve.

The interface is quiet, cool, and precise so the few moments that matter can be loud: a cue lighting the arm, a label swapping to a dish's ink, the record slowing to a stop at the finale. Color lives only in printed things (sleeves, labels, groove bands, label marks), and chrome stays in two inks on the plinth. Type is one family, Archivo, pulled to three widths: condensed heavy numerals you can read from across a kitchen, a normal width for instructions, and expanded caps for the lettering printed on labels.

Density is low and thumb-led. Each screen puts the disc at the top, one large statement under it, rows of dishes below, and the committing pill pinned at the bottom where a wet thumb reaches it. The world rejects recipe cards stacked with countdown timers and the album-art-plus-play-button music screen.
keyCharacteristics: One flat plinth ground; depth only from objects that sit on it (disc, arm, sleeves).
Two chrome inks (ink and ink-muted) plus one amber signal; dish inks printed only on record parts.
Archivo at three widths: condensed 62, normal 100, expanded 125.
Circles and pills for controls, 16dp soft rows, 4dp square sleeves.
Physical motion: damped springs, strong ease-out for UI, linear rotation locked to the beat clock.
Full light and dark themes that follow the system; Remove animations is honored.

rules.name: The Cue Light Rule
rules.body: Amber means "your hands, now" and nothing else: the lit cue lamp, the Done pill, and the hands-state dish pill. Never use it for decoration, selection, links, or brand emphasis.

rules.name: The Printed Ink Rule
rules.body: Dish inks appear only on record parts (sleeves, bands, labels, label marks, motif contours). Plinth, panels, chrome, and text stay in the neutral inks.

rules.name: The Named Ink Rule
rules.body: A dish's color is never its only identifier. Every label mark, sleeve, and band sits beside the instrument name, the dish name, or its track number (A1 to A5).

rules.name: The Two Themes Rule
rules.body: Every token has a light and a dark value chosen from the system setting; cue amber is the only color shared by both. Dynamic color is not used.

rules.name: The Three Widths Rule
rules.body: Condensed is for figures and the one display statement; normal is for anything read as a sentence; expanded is for short uppercase lettering only. Never set a sentence in condensed or expanded.

rules.name: The Tabular Time Rule
rules.body: Tabular figures are for time and nothing else: the countdown, cue times, readings, and dish-state pills. Numbers that change while watched never shift width.

rules.name: The sp Rule
rules.body: Every text size is in sp so it follows the system font scale; at font scale above 1.15 the Programme summary and its pill stack instead of sitting side by side.

rules.name: The Still Instruction Rule
rules.body: On Conduct the countdown sits in its own right-aligned slot beside the instruction, so the text being read never moves as the numbers change.

rules.name: The Thumb Bar Rule
rules.body: The one committing action on each screen ("Press the record", "Drop the needle", Done) is a pill pinned at the bottom, never at the top.

rules.name: The Objects Cast Rule
rules.body: Only the disc, the tonearm, and sleeves cast shadows. Pills, rows, cards, and tags stay flat.

rules.name: The Falloff Rule
rules.body: Shadows fade from a solid core to transparent. Never a hard offset copy of the shape.

rules.name: The Flat Plinth Rule
rules.body: The plinth is a flat fill. No brushed-metal texture, noise, or gradient on the ground; the only gradient on it is the bottom-bar fade back into plinth.

rules.name: The Three Radii Rule
rules.body: Pill for controls, 16dp for rows and cards, 4dp for sleeves. No other corner values.

dos: **Do** set every screen on the flat Aluminum Plinth and let the disc, arm, and sleeves be the only objects with depth.
**Do** reserve Cue Amber (#FFB21F) for the cue lamp, the Done pill, and the hands-state pill.
**Do** pair every dish ink with its instrument name, dish name, or track number.
**Do** use Archivo condensed for figures and the one display statement, normal for sentences, and expanded for short uppercase label lettering.
**Do** use tabular figures for every time value, and keep the countdown in its own slot so the instruction never moves.
**Do** keep to three radii: pills for controls, 16dp for rows and cards, 4dp for sleeves.
**Do** make every shadow a soft radial falloff that deepens in dark theme.
**Do** provide light and dark values for every new color and check `animationsEnabled()` before any decorative or long-running motion.
**Do** keep touch targets at 48dp or more and primary pills at 56dp, pinned at the thumb.
donts: **Don't** add brushed-metal texture, noise, or gradients to the plinth.
**Don't** use amber for selection, links, highlights, or brand color.
**Don't** paint dish inks onto panels, chrome, or text; they are printed on record parts only.
**Don't** let color alone tell dishes or dish states apart.
**Don't** use hard offset shadows or Material elevation on pills, rows, or cards.
**Don't** put small uppercase tags or eyebrows above headings; a statement stands on its own.
**Don't** set sentences in condensed or expanded widths, or use fixed px for text.
**Don't** enable dynamic color; the deck's inks replace the wallpaper palette.
